original_question: If an irreducible subvariety Z of A_g(C) contains a Zariski-dense set of complex multiplication points, must Z be of Hodge type?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 (Andre-Oort), specialized from a general Shimura variety Sh_K(G, X) to the moduli space A_g of principally polarized abelian varieties. The draft is aiming at the full conjectural statement, not the narrower proved case in Theorem 1.2, which only treats irreducible closed algebraic curves containing infinitely many special points with identical rational Hodge structure, and in particular curves containing infinitely many special points in one Hecke orbit. ([annals.math.princeton.edu](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v157-n2-p07.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already has the essential mathematical content right: the ambient space A_g(C), the relevant distinguished points (CM points, i.e. special points in this setting), the Zariski-density hypothesis inside an irreducible subvariety, and the expected conclusion that the subvariety should be of Hodge type. That is exactly the A_g-specialization of the Andre-Oort conjecture stated in Conjecture 1.1. ([annals.math.princeton.edu](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v157-n2-p07.pdf))
missing_details: Specify that g is a fixed positive integer and that A_g(C) denotes the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties of dimension g over C.
Say 'closed irreducible algebraic subvariety' rather than just 'irreducible subvariety,' to match the paper's algebraic-geometric formulation via Zariski closures and irreducible components.
Define 'CM points' as points corresponding to principally polarized abelian varieties of CM type; in the Shimura-variety language of the paper these are the special points.
Clarify that 'contains a Zariski-dense set of CM points' means dense in Z for the Zariski topology.
Use the paper's exact conclusion phrase 'subvariety of Hodge type' (equivalently, in later terminology, a special subvariety), rather than leaving that term implicit.

To match the official formulation most closely, the paper states the conjecture in terms of irreducible components of the Zariski closure of an arbitrary set of special points, rather than starting with a prechosen irreducible Z. ([annals.math.princeton.edu](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v157-n2-p07.pdf))

Paper-faithful scope: this is Conjecture 1.1, whereas Theorem 1.2 proves only a special case for curves with the extra hypothesis that all associated rational Hodge structures are isomorphic; in particular, it applies when the special points lie in one Hecke orbit. ([annals.math.princeton.edu](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v157-n2-p07.pdf))

Proposition 2.1 shows that, for proving the conjecture, one may reduce to the case where the Zariski closure is irreducible and Hodge generic; this is contextual precision from the nearby discussion, though it need not appear in the final stand-alone question. ([annals.math.princeton.edu](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v157-n2-p07.pdf))
refined_question: Fix an integer g >= 1, and let A_g(C) denote the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties of dimension g over C. If Z is a closed irreducible algebraic subvariety of A_g(C) whose complex points contain a Zariski-dense set of CM points (that is, points corresponding to principally polarized abelian varieties of CM type), must Z be a subvariety of Hodge type? ([annals.math.princeton.edu](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v157-n2-p07.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, by the reduction in Proposition 2.1, one may ask this only after passing to the smallest Shimura subvariety containing the closure, so that the Zariski closure of the CM points is assumed irreducible and Hodge generic. ([annals.math.princeton.edu](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v157-n2-p07.pdf))
justification: The draft is not trying to capture Theorem 1.2, because it does not impose the curve hypothesis or the stronger assumption that the special points have the same associated Q-Hodge structure or lie in one Hecke orbit. Those are exactly the extra hypotheses of the paper's proved special case. Instead, the draft matches the full conjectural statement Conjecture 1.1 after specializing from general Shimura varieties to A_g and from special points to CM points. Proposition 2.1 is the relevant nearby refinement because it explains the equivalent reduction to irreducible Hodge-generic closure. ([annals.math.princeton.edu](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v157-n2-p07.pdf))
